definition: Minimal recursion semantics (MRS) is a framework for computational semantics.
details: It can be implemented in typed feature structure formalisms such as head-driven phrase structure grammar and lexical functional grammar. It is suitable for computational language parsing and natural language generation. MRS enables a simple formulation of the grammatical constraints on lexical and phrasal semantics, including the principles of semantic composition. This technique is used in machine translation. Early pioneers of MRS include Ann Copestake, Dan Flickinger, Carl Pollard, and Ivan Sag.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. Think of it this way: Minimal recursion semantics (MRS) is a framework for computational semantics. And here is the clever part: It can be implemented in typed feature structure formalisms such as head-driven phrase structure grammar and lexical functional grammar. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. And that is Minimal recursion semantics — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
